about: The Fitness theme's genetic scores, read by nutrition.py --config fitness.json --prefix fit: per measure the GWAS Catalog traits (EFO) of its markers, Reactome pathways for the mechanism, the ClinVar conditions that count, and how it is measured. Each score is the genome-wide significant lead variants of one large GWAS, placed against 1000 Genomes Europeans. higher: whether a higher value is the good direction ('better', 'worse' or 'neutral'). meaning: what a low (20th percentile or below), typical or high (80th or above) score means in practice.

meaning.low: The genes start you on the weaker side. Strength responds to training from any starting point: heavy compound lifts two to three times a week close much of the gap.
meaning.typical: The genes put your starting strength near the middle. Training, protein and sleep decide where you end up.
meaning.high: The genes start you on the stronger side. A high starting point says little about how fast you gain, so build load gradually: tendons adapt slower than muscle.

meaning.low: The genes lean toward less muscle in the arms and legs. It builds the same way as for anyone, with progressive resistance training and protein spread over the day; it may take longer to show.
meaning.typical: The genes put your arm and leg muscle near the middle. Resistance training and protein decide the rest.
meaning.high: The genes lean toward more muscle in the arms and legs: you likely carry and keep muscle easily, which protects strength with age.

meaning.low: The genes lean toward less lean mass overall: muscle, organs and bone. Resistance training and enough protein matter more for you than for most.
meaning.typical: The genes put your overall lean mass near the middle.
meaning.high: The genes lean toward more lean mass overall, which goes with a higher resting energy use: you need more food to fuel training.

meaning.low: The genes lean toward a slower heart-rate drop after effort. Heart-rate recovery is one of the markers that improves most with endurance training: regular easy aerobic work and some intervals speed it up.
meaning.typical: The genes put your heart-rate recovery near the middle. It improves with endurance training.
meaning.high: The genes lean toward a fast heart-rate drop after effort, a sign of strong rest-and-digest control of the heart. A good base for endurance work.

meaning.low: The genes lean toward a smaller heart-rate rise during effort. Heart-rate zones from a formula may sit too high for you: set them from a test or from how hard the effort feels.
meaning.typical: The genes put your heart-rate rise during effort near the middle, so standard heart-rate zones should fit.
meaning.high: The genes lean toward a larger heart-rate rise during effort: the heart can speed up a lot to meet demand. Standard zones may read low for you.

meaning.low: The genes lean toward low creatine kinase: less muscle protein leaks into the blood after hard work.
meaning.typical: The genes put your creatine kinase near the middle.
meaning.high: The genes lean toward high creatine kinase: more muscle protein leaks into the blood after hard work. Expect more soreness after new or downhill and eccentric training; add volume gradually and give the same muscles 48 to 72 hours between hard sessions. A blood test taken within a few days of training can read high without anything being wrong.

tests.name: Caffeine

meaning.low: The genes lean toward drinking less coffee. Part of the genetics of coffee drinking is how fast the body clears caffeine, part how strongly you feel it; the CYP1A2 genotype below reads the clearance directly.
meaning.typical: The genes put your coffee drinking near the middle. The CYP1A2 genotype below says more about how fast you clear caffeine.
meaning.high: The genes lean toward drinking more coffee. Part of the genetics of coffee drinking is how fast the body clears caffeine, part how strongly you feel it; the CYP1A2 genotype below reads the clearance directly. Coffee drinking adds up: keep the last cup well before bedtime.

tests.test: Coffee intake (the GWAS measure); caffeine clearance itself is rarely tested
